_note: Anatomy defaults, the d20 band layout, and the one fixed location table (DESIGN.md §5.3, concept §5). The type→anatomy mapping is data rather than code so a world can disagree with it without a patch; per-actor overrides live in flags.pf1-critical-effects.anatomy / .beastLimbs / .appendages.
_dieNote: Hit location is a d20 (v2; it was a d12 through v1). The limb band is twelve faces wide so it divides evenly by 1, 2, 3 or 4 body parts, which is what lets beast and aberrant layouts be generated rather than enumerated.
_beastOrderNote: The order the checked beast categories fill the limb band in, whichever subset is checked. Also the full set of categories the checkboxes offer.
_maxAppendagesNote: How many appendage types an aberrant layout offers. Twelve divides evenly by every count up to this, which is the constraint on raising it (5 would not).
_byCreatureTypeNote: Keyed by PF1 creature type (pf1.config.creatureTypes). `beastLimbs` seeds the beast checkboxes, `appendages` the aberrant name fields — an empty string is an unnamed appendage, which reads as "Appendage". Only the list matching the mapped anatomy is used; the other is ignored.
_tablesNote: Only humanoid is a fixed table — its two limb categories are not a choice. Beast and aberrant are GENERATED from the creature's own layout (resolve/location.mjs), which is why they are absent here: their rows depend on which categories are checked, so there is no single table to write down. A layout with no limbs at all leaves the limb band unclaimed and the torso row grows to cover it.
